::: {.block title="Methods"}
We trained a separate model for each 10 m depth bin from the surface to 200 m to predict $\log_{10}(\mathrm{Chl}\,a)$ from $R_{rs}$ (11 or 172 bands), local solar hour, and sampling platform. We tried several model types (boosted regression trees, multilayer perceptrons, XGBoost); results here use boosted regression trees (BRT), which train quickly. Local solar hour allowed the model to account for daytime quenching of in situ chlorophyll fluorescence. Profiles were matched to the nearest cell of the same-day L3 $R_{rs}$ map. Skill is reported with SOCA2024's validation metrics (r², slope, MAPD, RMSD) and for integrated Chl *a*.

**Data leakage and validation.** Data leakage occurs when test observations are closely correlated in space or time with training observations, which inflates estimated skill. This was a critical issue for OOI moorings, which are fixed in space and give several samples a day that share one daily satellite pixel. To address data leakage, we grouped observations into 1° × 30-day space–time blocks and assigned each block to one of five cross-validation folds, repeated five times.
:::
